thread:
maria_cs: Hey team — Acme (canary account) is seeing a flurry of 429s during SDK init. Reported pattern: first 30s after deploy big spike, then trails off. They say this only happens when they route through their edge (Cloudflare HTTP/3 / QUIC).
eli_support: Thanks Maria — can you drop the request_id + sample logs? Also which SDK version?
maria_cs: request_id=rid_0b3f2a; sdk=0.10.1; region=eu-west-2; short log snippet: `2026-03-21T10:12:01Z rid_0b3f2a INIT start; 2026-03-21T10:12:02Z rid_0b3f2a 429 preflight; x-retry-after: 2s; tcp_conn: quic; src: cloudflare`
acme-sre: FYI we do a parallel init on every lambda coldstart (concurrency=12 by default). We tried lowering but still see bursts when there are many lambdas. Also seeing TTLs for ephemeral token are ~8s on our side due to clock skew.
jen_devx: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) preflight concurrency + no jitter -> stampede on ephemeral token refresh; (2) HTTP/3 QUIC proxies dropping or rewriting headers used for upstream routing, causing backend to treat many as unauthenticated -> 429s.
alex_backend: +1. If the proxy is rewriting upstream sockets, the connection reuse semantics change and our rate limiter (per-conn heuristic) misattributes load. Also if X-Forwarded-For / Via gets truncated some rate keys collide.
sre-bot: alert: canary-account-acme preflight-429-rate 2026-03-21T10:12:02Z -> 10s window: 87 events, 90th p90 latency 340ms
eli_support: Can you try two quick things: 1) reduce init parallelism to 2 and add jitter 0..500ms on init calls; 2) re-run with HTTP/3 disabled at Cloudflare (falls back to HTTP/2) and report if 429s disappear?
acme-sre: Will try now. Quick note — our ephemeral token rotate logic does `if token.expires_in < 5s then refresh()` which may race at scale. We can add a randomized backoff.
maria_cs: attached a tiny repro patch suggestion for them:
```
// pseudocode: staggered init
for i in 0..concurrency-1 {
  sleep(random(0, jitter_ms))
  parallel_init()
}
```
Set concurrency=2, jitter_ms=500.
jen_devx: Also recommend using the SDK env var: `REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_MAX_PARALLEL=2` and `REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_JITTER_MS=250` — that'll flip instantly for them. We should add a note in onboarding doc about HTTP/3 proxies and preflight semantics.
acme-sre: Quick test results: after disabling HTTP/3 we see 429s drop by ~92% in the first minute. With concurrency=2+jitter we have clean start. Looks like both fixes help.
eli_support: Great. Action items: 1) Maria: send config snippet + one-click SDK env recommendation to customer (help article link). 2) Alex: open runtime ticket to mark headers used for rate keys as authoritative and add safer fallback when Via/XFF is truncated. 3) DevEx: add short blurb to onboarding checklist about edge proxies (HTTP/3) and preflight concurrency. 4) SRE: keep monitoring p90 for next 24h for canary account.
maria_cs: will do. Scheduling a 30m follow-up with Acme tomorrow to confirm renewal health — propose 10:30am UTC. :thumbsup:
acme-sre: Thanks all, that plan sounds good. We'll keep HTTP/3 disabled for now while we validate.
jen_devx: I'll draft the onboarding blurb and link to the quick mitigations page.
eli_support: Closing loop here — put the ticket in `cs/onboard/needs-runtime-fix` and ping me once alex posts the runtime ticket id.
alex_backend: will open RUN-4829 with logs and a hypothesis section.
sre-bot: note: continuing to sample metrics — will surface a follow-up alert if rates go above threshold.
